Your social life is defined as “the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working”. It’s important to have a social life, but what’s right for one person won’t be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, [1] some of us may feel drained, even if it’s doing something we enjoy.

This is why finding a [2] in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not [3] others, can make you feel lonely and [4]. Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and [5] a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, [6], you are working from home and you are [7] on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can [8] periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.

It’s important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to [9] a social life, but it can feel overwhelming [10]. It’s a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet [11] people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to [12] a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and [13] ideas.

On the other hand, it’s [14] possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you’re always doing something and there is never any [15] in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social [16]. We all have our own social limit and it’s important to recognise when you’re feeling like it’s all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be [17] of poor social health. Make sure you [18] some time in your diary when you’re [19] for socialising and use this time to relax, [20] and recover.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. “Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes. “An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”

Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can’t be expected to embrace the changes if they’re not seeing the benefits—if they’re just seeing good jobs being destroyed.

In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech’s inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. “We’re talking about disruption,” she says. “These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.” To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.

Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.

According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings’s Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.

The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.

Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.

A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don’t simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country’s reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 per cent of the UK’s wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.

Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don’t go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. “Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood,” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. “For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.”

The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 per cent. The causes of the UK’s current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels. It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects.

While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK’s net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall added: “While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net zero.”

“While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground. Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.”

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it’s time to turn over the keys. “It’s a complete life-changer” when someone stops—or is forced to stop—driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.

“The American Medical Association advises physicians that ‘in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician’s advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,’” Menke wrote. “Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality,” she counseled.

Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. “There’s not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said. “We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.

One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.

Many older drivers don’t see eye doctors or can’t afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can’t turn their heads or remember where they are going—or have gotten shorter and haven’t changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.

As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won’t solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. “If we’re going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health—and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.

While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors’ offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically does not receive the same legal protections.

Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that “despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users’ sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties.” Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users’ express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.

Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company’s privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.

As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
How Colleges Weigh Applicants’ Extracurricular Activities

High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission to a selective undergraduate institution. However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful’s extracurricular activities matters more than the number of activities he or she participates in.

Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application. “No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurriculars that they have been passionately involved in each for an extended period of time,” Rexford wrote in an email.

Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity. “The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they’re going to do a popular activity, I’d say, be the best at it,” says Sara Harberson, a college admissions consultant.

High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say. “For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skill and potential by starting a profitable small business,” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.

Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland high school guidance counselor, says unconventional extracurricular activities can help students impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated serious commitment. “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique?,’ having an uncommon extracurricular activity vs. a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.

Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions. “Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley, admissions counselor at IvyWise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email. “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”

Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest. “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.

High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与句内对比逻辑。
［解题思路］前分句指出“一些人会因与他人共度大量时光而精力充沛（feel energised）”，后分句转而表明“另一些人即便是在做自己喜爱之事时，也可能感到精疲力竭（feel drained）”。两者主系表结构平行且情绪截然相反，故需选用表达对比转折关系的连词 whereas（而、却），故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］because（因为）强加因果；［B］unless（除非）表示否定条件；［D］until（直到……为止）表时间终点，误将两类对立人群当作同一群人的先后状态转变。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与全篇核心主旨。
［解题思路］首段指明同一种社交体验于不同人利弊各异；下文紧接着分别剖析“独处过多（社交过少）造成孤独”与“社交过度引发倦怠疲劳”。可见全篇主旨围绕如何在两端之间寻求合理均衡展开，空格句作为中心主旨句，意为“在社交生活中找到平衡（[2] balance）至关重要”，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］contrast（差异、对比）干扰来自前段人群对比，但寻找差异不合全篇“调和适度”的建议主旨；［C］link（联系、纽带）常与 between 搭配；［D］gap（缺口、分歧）均背离均衡主线。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内取舍结构与常见动词熟词僻义。
［解题思路］主语部分为否定对照结构：花太多时间独处（Spending too much time on your own），即“不与他人会面交往（not [3] others）”。see 后接人时意为“会面、来往、与……相处”，精确对应“缺少人际往来”的孤立状态，故选［A］seeing。
［错项排除］［B］pleasing（取悦他人）带有迎合色彩，偏离客观陈述日常交往；［C］judging（评判他人）与［D］teaching（教导他人）均无法与前文的“花过多时间独处”构成直接的语义反面对应。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列结构与情感形容词辨析。
［解题思路］句中 feel lonely and [4] 由并列连词 and 连接两个充当表语的消极心理形容词，共同描摹过度独处给人带来的负面体会。disconnected 意为“与外界脱离联系的、孤立无援的、脱节的”，精准贴合社交缺失带来的孤独隔绝感，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］misguided（被误导的、糊涂的）、［B］surprised（惊讶的）及［C］spoiled（被宠坏的/破坏的）均无法与 lonely 构成同向语义并列。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内因果并列逻辑与动词短语辨析。
［解题思路］主语为 Loneliness（孤独感），and 连接两个并列不定式成分作补足语：“已知孤独不仅会损害你的心理健康（impact on your mental health），还会促成、导致低落情绪（[5] a low mood）”。contribute to 表示“引起、促成、导致”，与前面负面影响顺理成章构成并列，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］rely on（依赖、依靠）受前面介词 on 结构干扰，但逻辑主被动完全错位；［C］interfere with（妨碍、干扰）带入后意为“孤独妨碍好心情”尚可，但与负面名词 a low mood 搭配变为“阻碍低落情绪”，反向违背文意；［D］go against（违背、与……作对）同样与“加重负面情绪”相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句间例证关系与高频插入短语辨析。
［解题思路］前句泛指“任何人在任何时候都可能感到孤独”，空格句以 This（这种情况）回指前文，并具体描绘“当你居家办公从而错失办公室社交”这一典型场景。因此逗号隔开的插入语用于引出具体实例，for example（例如）最合句意，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］in fact（事实上）多用于修正或反驳前文预期；［B］of course（当然）表理所当然的让步；［D］on average（平均而言）用于量化统计语境，三者均无法承担由泛指到具体个例的例证衔接功能。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义逻辑与动词短语搭配。
［解题思路］条件从句通过并列结构描绘居家办公状态：“你在家办公（working from home）并且你正在[7]办公室里习惯发生的日常社交互动（the usual social conversations that happen in an office）”。物理隔离导致无法参与公司茶水间或走廊闲聊，miss out on 表示“错失、错过（良机或益事）”，恰如其分，故选［B］missing out。
［错项排除］［A］cutting back on（削减经费或用量）暗示主动减量，而居家办公令办公室现场寒暄直接无法发生；［C］breaking in on（强行闯入打断对话）及［D］looking down on（轻视、蔑视）语义与场景严重冲突。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句际并列逻辑与动词辨析。
［解题思路］空格句紧接“居家办公极易诱发孤独”一例，以句尾 too（也）表示并列补充：“其他生活变故——例如退休、换工作或初为人父母——同样可能[8]一阵阵孤独期（periods of loneliness）”。trigger（触发、引发）形象传达重大人生节点诱发阶段性孤独的因果链条，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］shorten（缩短）和［D］interrupt（打断、中止）均与前句引出孤独成因的方向截然相反；［C］follow（跟随在……之后）逻辑颠倒，是生活变故引发孤独而非单纯时序尾随。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文呼应与动宾搭配。
［解题思路］第三段转入“面对孤独如何破局”的实用建议。在强调“意识到这些孤独感很重要”后，作者指出“存在多种办法能帮助你重拾、恢复（[9]）社交生活（a social life）”，并随后依次展开从兴趣爱好切入的具体方案，故选［D］regain（重新获得、重拾）。
［错项排除］［A］assess（评估）与［B］interpret（诠释、理解）对象重在评价或解读已有事物；［C］provide（提供）通常无法与个人自身“重新过上社交生活”直接构成自反语义（provide a social life 多指组织为他人提供社交场合）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句际“问题—策略”顺承与介词短语。
［解题思路］句内指出重拾社交生活的方法虽然很多，“但这在[10]（一开始、起初）或许让人感到不知所措”；紧接着下句给出破冰第一招：“从思考你喜欢的兴趣爱好开始（start by...）是个好主意”。at first 与下句 start 构成天然呼应，描绘万事开头难但有法可循的逻辑，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］in turn（依次、继而）、［C］on time（准时地）和［D］by chance（偶然地）均无法回应下句专门针对“最初起步（start by）”的循序指导。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文顺承与复合形容词辨析。
［解题思路］承接“思考个人兴趣爱好”的起步建议，作者指出接着去参加相关的兴趣社团或活动，在那里你就能结识“志趣相投的（[11]）”朋友。like-minded（志同道合的、有相同兴趣爱好的）严密贴合“因共同爱好相聚”的社团属性，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］far-sighted（有远见的）、［B］strong-willed（意志坚定的）和［C］kind-hearted（心地善良的）虽然均属褒义品质形容词，但皆非依托特定共同爱好拓展交际圈所聚焦的筛选纽带。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与并列对照。
［解题思路］本句与前面的 aimed at new parents（针对新手父母）并列，共同列举初次开启新体验的社群类别：“针对那些想要生平第一次[12]一项新运动的人（[12] a new sport for the first time）”。try 意为“尝试、试一试”，贴合新手初次体验的动作特征，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］promote（推广、促销）多为资深参与者或组织方职责；［C］watch（观看体育比赛）属旁观而非亲身融入社团练习；［D］describe（描述）脱离参与式运动社团语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列搭配与社交语境。
［解题思路］末分句举例面向同行举办的行业交流活动（networking events），目的是让业内人士聚在一起并“[13]观点、分享想法（meet up and [13] ideas）”。share ideas 为极其地道的并列高频搭配，凸显同行线下交流互通有无的价值，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］test（测试想法）偏重严谨实验或调研；［C］accept（接受）侧重单方被动认可；［D］revise（修改观点）均不符轻松互通信息的职场交流场合。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段际转折并列逻辑与副词辨析。
［解题思路］第二、三段剖析“社交过少”的孤独困扰及应对，第四段开篇以 On the other hand（另一方面）切换视角，指出社交过度同样是客观风险——“另一方面，过度社交[14]是可能的（it's [14] possible to have too much of a social life）”。also（也、同样）承前启后引出另一端失衡状况，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］already（已经）与探讨普遍客观可能性不符；［B］thus（因此）错误构建了因果推论；［D］only（仅仅）排除了前两段刚刚讨论过的“社交匮乏”这一半边问题。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列与名词语法词义辨析。
［解题思路］条件从句指出：若你觉得自己仿佛永远都在连轴转，并且在日程表（calendar）里从未给休整闲暇时间留出过任何“[15]（空隙、空白时段）”。space 作为不可数名词恰可紧跟否定句中的 any，表示日程表中可供喘息的“余地/空白时段”，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］list（清单）作“清单”解通常为可数单数，不可直接置于 never any 后，且“没列闲暇清单”不等同“日程排满无空”；［B］order（顺序、条理）及［D］boundary（边界）亦无法在日程格（calendar）内形象表达预留可支配空闲区域之意。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列逻辑与名词词义辨析。
［解题思路］句内 or 连接两个意义相近的负面状态：如果你日程毫无空档，就可能遭受“社交耗竭（social burnout）”或者“社交[16]（疲劳、倦怠）”。fatigue（极度疲惫、劳累）与 burnout 构成精准近义呼应，指出过量社交对精力的消耗，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］criticism（批评、指责）、［C］injustice（不公正）与［D］dilemma（进退两难的困境）皆侧重外部人际摩擦或道德冲突，而非连续赶场社交导致的个人身心倦怠。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文顺承与名词语义辨析。
［解题思路］前句刚刚呼吁“要能察觉自己何时快到承受极限”，紧接着本句列举四个典型临床表现——“情绪低落、精力枯竭、烦躁易怒以及失眠”都可能是社交健康亮红灯的“[17]（迹象、征兆）”。signs of poor social health 贴切承担由表象诊断状态的作用，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］sources（根源、来源）颠倒因果——失眠等是过度社交导致的结果症状而非病因；［B］standards（标准）与［D］scores（分数）均不用于指代身体不适表现。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文对应与动词短语搭配。
［解题思路］针对前文“日程表中毫无空隙”引发的社交耗竭，作者在本段末给出可操作性建议：务必在日程本（in your diary）上专门“[18]（划出、标记出）”留给自己休整的一段专属时光。mark out 意为“划定界线、特别标出（时间段）”，精准呼应“在日程表留白”，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］take over（接管、占满日程）反而挤压空白；［B］wipe off（擦掉涂抹表面）多指清除污渍，或完全消灭；［C］add up（累加计算）不构成从忙碌日程中“划分预留独处时段”的操作含义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与形容词搭配。
［解题思路］既然这段划出的独处时光旨在“用来放松和恢复”，那就意味着在这段时间里，你对于一切社交邀约处于“[19]（谢绝参与的、无暇应酬的）”状态（when you're unavailable for socialising）。unavailable 正是指对外界发出“此刻不予安排社交”的谢客信号，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］ungrateful（忘恩负义的）与社交休息毫无干系；［C］responsible（负责任的）与［D］regretful（遗憾懊悔的）皆无法准确界定这段“对外关闭社交通道”的物理状态。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列结构与动作收尾。
［解题思路］最后一句以三个并列不定式说明预留独处空档的用途：“用这段时间来放松（relax）、[20]以及休养恢复（recover）”。rest（休息、歇息）与前后两个动词词性、声韵及语义方向完全一致，共绘闭环调节图景，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］react（作出反应，常需接 to）、［B］repeat（重复）以及［C］return（返回、归还）均无法与 relax、recover 并肩表示从过度社交疲劳中抽身休整。

questions.stem: Coyle argues in her new book that economic growth should
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（著作主旨与分配正义定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Coyle argues in her new book 与 economic growth 定位至第一段。作者援引剑桥经济学家 Diane Coyle 的新书观点指出：若想避免政治秩序分崩离析，经济增长的成果必须比近年来更公平地分享给大众（the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past）。选项［C］benefit people equally 精准同义改写 more evenly shared，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］催生创新、［B］使职业选择多元化及［D］强力推动经济增速均将“成果分配更加均衡”的政治经济警告偷换为创新手段或单纯总量扩张，偏离首段关切。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, digital technologies should be used to
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（Paragraph 2 措施定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 2 与 digital technologies 定位至第二段。首句指出：Coyle 认为提升大众生活水平与富足度需要更广泛地运用数字技术，以提高各经济领域的生产效率（to boost productivity in various sectors），从而遏制不平等扩大。选项［C］raise overall work efficiency 是对 boost productivity in various sectors 的标准同义转述，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］带来瞬间繁荣过度夸大（原文用 improving 并强调需长期配套变革）；［B］减轻工作量将“提高生产率”误读为让人少干活；［D］加强跨行业协作在第二段未有论述。

questions.stem: What does Coyle fear about transformative technologies?

options.text: They may be impractical to deploy.
options.content: They may be impractical to deploy.

options.text: They may be unwelcome to the public.
options.content: They may be unwelcome to the public.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物态度与担忧定位题。
［精准定位］根据题干询问 Coyle 对变革性技术的担忧，定位至第三、四段。第三段指出若想让人们接受颠覆性变化，社会认同（social buy-in）至关重要；第四段紧接转折指出许多人心头怨气正在暗涌（resentment is simmering among many），并进一步补充人们担忧好工作被摧毁、自己反而受害。这些均说明她担心变革性技术得不到公众欢迎甚至遭遇抵制，故［D］They may be unwelcome to the public 正确。
［错项排除］［A］影响工作生活平衡与［C］产生巨额财政开支在两段均未涉及；［B］部署不切实际偷换了民众情感排斥与技术落地可行性的概念。

questions.stem: Several American cities are mentioned to show

options.text: the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US.
options.content: the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US.

options.text: the disappointing prospect of tech jobs in the US.
options.content: the disappointing prospect of tech jobs in the US.

options.text: the fast progress of US regional economies.
options.content: the fast progress of US regional economies.

options.text: the increasing significance of US AI assets.
options.content: the increasing significance of US AI assets.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］例证目的题（例证结构前后关联定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Several American cities 定位至第五、六段。第五段列举旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿等寥寥数座城市便吸纳了全美约三分之二的人工智能相关资产（two-thirds of the nation's AI assets）；第六段首句立即点破该例证的核心论证意图：少数城市的垄断主导地位意味着财富的地域失衡（geographical disparities in wealth）将继续加剧。可见举例意在凸显 AI 技术在美国地理分布上的高度不均，故［A］the uneven distribution of AI technologies in the US 正确。
［错项排除］［B］对美国科技就业前景感到失望与文本呼吁重塑应用方向相悖；［C］区域经济快速发展及［D］AI 资产日益重要均把少数城市的极端集中误当作全美普遍态势或重点偏离。

questions.stem: With regard to Coyle’s concern, the author suggests

options.text: raising funds to start new AI projects.
options.content: raising funds to start new AI projects.

options.text: guarding against the side effects of AI.
options.content: guarding against the side effects of AI.

options.text: redefining the role of AI technologies.
options.content: redefining the role of AI technologies.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］作者观点与建议定位题（末段收束定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Coyle's concern 与 author suggests 定位至文章最后一段。作者借对“只关心替代人工而漠视分配公平”的反思指出：我们需要拓宽数字想象力（broaden our digital imaginations），重新构想那些不只是淘汰岗位的 AI 技术，让它们在人类与机械各自擅长的领域里扩展新机遇（expand opportunities）。这实质是主张重新界定人工智能技术的社会功能定位，故［D］redefining the role of AI technologies 正确。
［错项排除］［A］筹资开启新项目与［B］鼓励 AI 科研合作在末段均无着落；［C］防范 AI 副作用泛泛而谈，未能切中作者提倡“赋能扩展机会而非单一替代人工”的建设性转折主旨。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the UK needs to

options.text: lift its control on timber imports.
options.content: lift its control on timber imports.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（首段核心问题定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 UK needs to 定位至第一段。英国木材行业协会 Confor 呼吁采取紧急行动减少对进口木材的依赖（reduce the country's reliance on timber imports）并提供稳定供应，因目前建筑用材仅 20% 为本国自产（home-grown），英国沦为全球第二大木材净进口国。由此清晰可知英国急需增加国内木材供应，故［A］increase its domestic wood supply 正确。
［错项排除］［B］削减木材需求与建筑环保减碳急需大批用材的现实相反；［C］降低生产成本及［D］解除进口管制在首段均无提及（文中反而是担忧过度依赖进口）。

questions.stem: According to Confor, the UK government’s fresh incentives

options.text: can hardly address a construction crisis.
options.content: can hardly address a construction crisis.

options.text: are believed to come at a wrong time.
options.content: are believed to come at a wrong time.

options.text: seem to be misleading for landowners.
options.content: seem to be misleading for landowners.

options.text: will be too costly to put into practice.
options.content: will be too costly to put into practice.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点细节题（行业机构对现行政策的评估）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Confor 与 fresh incentives 定位至第二段首句。在提及政府于气候减排计划下最新宣布的鼓励植树政策（fresh incentives for tree planting）后，Confor 负责人直言“但这些举措远远不够（don't go far enough），未能有效倡导植树造林提升木材供给的益处”，而前段首句已警示英国正因缺林少木面临未来建筑危机（a future construction crisis）。可见这些新激励远远不足以化解建筑危机，故［A］can hardly address a construction crisis 正确。
［错项排除］［B］时机不当将政策力度不足错改成了时间节点错误；［C］误导土地所有者在第二段并未指明；［D］推行成本高昂在后文未曾讨论。

questions.stem: The UK’s exposure to fluctuating wood prices is a result of

options.text: the government’s inaction on timber imports.
options.content: the government’s inaction on timber imports.

options.text: the competition among timber traders at home.
options.content: the competition among timber traders at home.

options.text: wood producers’ motive to maximise profits.
options.content: wood producers’ motive to maximise profits.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］因果细节题（历史成因追踪定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 exposure to fluctuating wood prices 定位至第二段末句。Confor 负责人指出：几十年来我们始终未担负起投资本土木材供应的责任（have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply），致使国家轻易暴露在动荡的国际市场价格与供应链断裂风险之下。Options 中［B］inadequate investment in growing wood（对林木种植投资不足）精准对应原文未投资本土供材的历史短板，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］对木材进口的无所作为将缺口根源“本土缺投资”偷换为“政府不管进口”；［C］国内木材贸易商竞争及［D］逐利动机均属无中生有。

questions.stem: Which of the following causes the shortage of wood supply in the UK?

options.text: Outdated technologies of the wood industry.
options.content: Outdated technologies of the wood industry.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（行业供应链障碍定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干询问英国木材短缺的成因，定位至第三段末句。该段分析缺木的多重原因，其中不仅涉及审批制度与技术培训滞后，最后还特别指出农民及其他土地所有者对投资长期植树项目顾虑重重、犹豫不决（significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in longer-term planting projects）。选项［D］Farmers' unwillingness to plant trees 准确提炼这一主观畏难障碍，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］建筑业木材消耗过量与第一段提倡木结构减排环保趋势冲突；［B］自然种植条件不利与英国气候宜林（第二段仅说人为投资失责）不符；［C］木材行业技术过时曲解了原文“培训技术工人以助植树（training people to help plant them）”的表述。

questions.stem: What does Goodall think the UK government should do?

options.text: Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes.
options.content: Subsidise the building of low-carbon homes.

options.text: Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies.
options.content: Pay greater attention to boosting rural economies.

options.text: Provide more support for productive tree planting.
options.content: Provide more support for productive tree planting.

options.text: Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy.
options.content: Give priority to pursuing its net-zero strategy.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物观点题（对策诉求总结定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干人名 Goodall 定位至第四、五段。Goodall 在第四段批判政府现行扶持只聚焦于粮食生产和专为生物多样性服务的野生原始林，而忽略了具有生产力的商业林业（productive forestry）；第五段他紧接着强调必须借助合理政策推动更多生产性树木的栽种（greater impetus to the vision of planting more productive trees），为建筑与制造业提供稳固资源。可见他认为英国政府应加大对生产性植树的扶持，故［C］Provide more support for productive tree planting 正确。
［错项排除］［A］直接补贴低碳建房及［B］重在促进乡村经济虽有附带词根联系（如 rural economies），但并非 Goodall 向政府提出的核心林政呼吁；［D］将净零排放置于最优先偏离其强调具体产木政策的重心。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road

options.text: can be a tough task to complete.
options.content: can be a tough task to complete.

options.text: will be beneficial to their health.
options.content: will be beneficial to their health.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（首段核心难点定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 unsafe aging drivers off the road 定位至第一段首句。文中开篇明义：让高龄不安全驾驶者停止开车（keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road）面临的最大挑战之一（One of the biggest challenges），就是说服他们接受是时候交出车钥匙了——而对许多人来说这形同丧失独立生活能力。biggest challenges 直接对应选项［C］can be a tough task to complete（是一项难以完成的棘手任务），故正确。
［错项排除］［A］称其为新安全举措与“长期以来都是棘手挑战”及后文多年争议不符；［B］成为争议话题在首段未强调（首段聚焦说服老人本身的心理困难而非政策争论）；［D］有益健康同样未在首段阐述。

questions.stem: The American Medical Association’s advice
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（各州对行业建议的态度对比）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 American Medical Association's advice 定位至第二段。文中指出美国医学会虽建议医生一旦认为某患者不再适宜驾车即应予以报告（physicians report when they think a patient is no longer fit to drive），但各州立法却五花八门：有的州强制规定医生汇报，有的允许但不强求，少数州甚至视之为违反医患保密原则的侵权行为。显然该建议在各地遭遇截然不同的反应，故［D］has met with different responses 正确。
［错项排除］［A］赢得驾驶员普遍支持在文中无据（连医生和州立法都意见不一）；［B］普遍被视为不现实及［C］被广泛斥为多余皆过度概括（实际上不少州已采用并强行要求上报）。

questions.stem: According to Dugan, efforts to keep older drivers safe
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］观点推断题（问题症结概括定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干人名 Dugan 与关键词 older drivers safe 定位至第三段。专家 Elizabeth Dugan 抱怨道，当下老年人行车安全难题只是由各个专注点不同的行业分支“零敲碎打（addressed piecemeal）”地各自应付——“我们甚至没有一个全国老年驾驶研究机构”；她指出我们需要从全局顶层加以统筹改进。由此推断有关安全措施亟待良好协调与整合，故［B］need to be well coordinated 正确。
［错项排除］［A］带来了巨大变化与现状停滞破碎相反；［C］已获得公众认可及［D］急需专门法律支持均脱离她批评“各行其是、缺乏顶层研究统筹机构”的核心论点。

questions.stem: Some older drivers have trouble driving because they tend to
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］因果细节题（驾驶困难生理原因定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干提问部分老人驾车困难的原因，定位至第五段。该段第二句直接道出常见诱因：一些老年人在驾车时感到吃力，是因为他们无法灵活转头，或是不记得自己正要开往哪里（can't turn their heads or remember where they are going），或是反应速度变慢而无法躲避危险。其中“记不起目的地”正体现记忆力衰退，故［B］have a weakened memory 正确。
［错项排除］［A］固守坏驾驶习惯、［C］忍受慢性疼痛以及［D］忽视汽车日常保养在原文第五段生理与认知退化说明中均无根据。

questions.stem: Dugan thinks that the solution to the problems of crashes may lie in

options.text: adjusting the age limit for drivers.
options.content: adjusting the age limit for drivers.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物观点题（末段未来汽车设计方案定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干人名 Dugan 与 solution to the problems of crashes 定位至文章最后一段。谈及如何减少涉及老龄司机的恶性碰撞事故，Dugan 直言：我们必须着眼于设计制造适应寿命延长时代的交通工具——“既然人能活到百岁，我们就需要打造出 90 岁老人都能自如舒适驾驶的汽车（cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably）”。选项［B］developing senior-friendly cars 准确转述，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］单纯升级完全自动驾驶车偏离原文“让 90 岁老人亲手舒适安全驾车”的设计理念；［C］翻新交通基础设施及［D］调整司机法定驾龄上限在末段均未主张。

questions.stem: The research findings are cited in Paragraph 1 to show
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］例证目的题（数据支撑现象定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 research findings 与 Paragraph 1 定位至第一段。文章首句即指出手机里往往装着不止一款健康类 APP，随即通过调研机构数据（2021 年市面上有逾 35 万款健康应用，仅 2020 年就上线 9 万款）予以量化夯实。引用庞大增长数据意在生动展示如今健康类 APP 的极度普及与盛行，故［A］the prevalence of health apps 正确。
［错项排除］［B］公众对健康的高度担忧及［C］智能手机本身的普及率均偏离例证主体“健康应用程序的数量爆炸与普及”；［D］泛言科技进步同样不如［A］紧扣全篇聚焦的健康应用监管主题。

questions.stem: What does the author imply about existing health privacy law?

options.text: Its coverage needs to be extended.
options.content: Its coverage needs to be extended.

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］推理判断题（现行医疗隐私法规漏洞定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干询问作者对现有健康隐私法律的暗示，定位至第二段。该段指出如 HIPAA 等现行法律严格规范传统医院、诊所、药房及医保商，但这些新兴健康 APP 与科技公司所采集的海量个人健康数据却通常无法享受到同等的法律保护（typically does not receive the same legal protections）。由此合理推出，现有健康隐私法案覆盖面过窄，亟待扩展完善以涵盖新应用，故［A］Its coverage needs to be extended 正确。
［错项排除］［B］执法力度需加强将“法律压根没覆盖管辖新应用”曲解为原有条文执行不力；［C］遏制了医疗不当行为及［D］令保险公司失望均无正文依据。

questions.stem: Before sharing its users’ health information, Flo Health is required to

options.text: seek the approval of the FTC
options.content: seek the approval of the FTC

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（典型判例监管要求定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Flo Health 与 sharing its users' health information 定位至第三段末句。在联邦贸易委员会（FTC）对生殖健康经期跟踪应用 Flo Health 违约向脸书等第三方泄露用户私密数据的执法和解中，FTC 强制要求该公司在今后分享任何用户健康信息前，必须事先取得用户的“明示肯定同意（get app users' express affirmative consent）”。选项［D］obtain their explicit permission（获取明确许可）精准对应，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］须先获得 FTC 逐案审批将原本“须征得用户本人明确同意”的主体错换成监管机构；［B］寻找合资格第三方及［C］清除无关个人资料均违背法律强调的授权前置原则。

［考点提炼］细节理解题（监管机构现实困境定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干询问 FTC 当前面临的挑战，定位至第四段末句。文中首先说明 FTC 的职责涵盖防止行业普遍存在的欺骗与不公平行为，随后紧接着强调：但这些健康 APP 铺天盖地涌向市场的惊人速度本身，便足见这一监管挑战是何等巨大（the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is）。选项［B］The rapid increase in new health apps 直接照应前句新应用飙升速度，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］健康信息本身的复杂性、［C］应用的隐蔽欺诈性与［D］难以量化消费者损害虽可能属实务难点，但本段末句指出的具体巨量挑战明确定格于“高速涌入市场的新应用浪潮”。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段落推断题（地方立法推进概括）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 last paragraph 与 health data protection 定位至末段。文中指出加州率先通过消费者隐私法案等立法保障本州居民信息安全，而弗吉尼亚、科罗拉多和犹他等州也已接连效仿跟进出台隐私法律。这说明个人健康信息与数据隐私保护已率先在多州赢得明确立法支持，故［D］has gained legislative support in some states 正确。
［错项排除］［A］已受到 APP 开发者普遍拥护违背文中开发者常暗自违约牟利的现象；［B］已成为联邦层面的立法核心恰与前文缺乏联邦层面涵盖 APP 的法律现实矛盾；［C］在加州遭遇强烈阻力与“加州领衔出台隐私保护法”正好相反。
